safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not explicitly state the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the headache was still present during the consult can blur the acuity and trajectory (persistent vs resolved), which may affect follow-up urgency and response-to-treatment assessment. In most cases it leads to inefficiency or less precise clinical reasoning rather than direct harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact mentions absence of neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key red-flag feature when evaluating acute headache (e.g., meningitis/SAH); omitting a documented negative can make it unclear whether this was assessed and could prompt unnecessary escalation or repeat questioning. Because the true finding is a reassuring negative, the likely impact is limited, but the domain is higher-risk.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No NKDA/allergy status is present in generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting allergy status (NKDA) is clinically important because it can lead to inadvertent prescribing/administration of an allergen, particularly when recommending medications like NSAIDs/aspirin. Even if the patient truly has no allergies, the absence of this safety check increases downstream risk.
